title: Orchestrate PRD sign-offs for private upgrade & RBAC model-pinning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket coordinates cross-team review and formal acceptance for the PRD that defines the Private Deployment upgrade path and RBAC-first model-pinning feature. The PRD proposes: (1) an in-place upgrade mechanism for private tenants, (2) model-version pinning controls surfaced in console with role-based access, and (3) audit logging + KMS integration for pinned-model artifacts.

Why now: Several enterprise customers requested predictable upgrade behavior and explicit model pinning to comply with internal change-control policies. The Private product release (private-2025.10) depends on aligned sign-offs from Engineering, Design, and Legal to unblock implementation sprints and customer pilots.

Scope: Clarify and lock the following PRD areas before development tickets are scheduled:
- exact semantics of "model pinning" (per-route vs per-tenant vs per-deployment)
- console UX for pin creation/editing and RBAC controls
- migration strategy for existing pinned and unpinned routes
- required audit fields and KMS key handling for on-prem and VPC installs
- contract / data residency constraints that affect private upgrades and pinned artifact storage

Deliverables:
- Signed PRD with explicit acceptance criteria (this ticket)
- Eng implementation RFC and test plan linked below
- Design mockups with microcopy and error states linked below
- Legal checklist confirming contract language and export/residency constraints

Success measure: PRD has approvals from ENG, DESIGN, and LEGAL by due_date and no open blockers that would change scope. Once approved, engineering may schedule implementation work in the next internal sprint cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering has reviewed and annotated the PRD and resolved open technical questions listed in the PRD (migration path, backward compatibility, canary strategy).
Design has provided final console mockups for pin creation/editing, RBAC role mappings, and error/confirmation states; accessibility review completed.
Legal certifies that contract language covering pinned-model custody, export controls, and data residency is available or that a mitigation plan is documented.
A test matrix exists mapping acceptance tests to criteria: unit/integration for migration, e2e for console flows, and an incident rollback plan.
All dependencies (ENG-2891, DES-121, LEGAL-57) are either closed or have documented milestones and mitigations before implementation starts.
